variants.headline: Union calls a strike
variants.sub: A strike has been called by the union {name}.
variants.body:
The union {name} has called a strike. The call establishes a labour action, not an account of its participation or outcome. Readers considering {target} should distinguish the decision to call a strike from unreported claims about wages, conditions or the response of an employer.

A strike call requires attention to labour relations without a fabricated estimate of lost output. Managers should distinguish the declaration from its practical extent and duration. A disciplined commercial view can take bargaining seriously while refusing to turn an unspecified action into a precise forecast of costs or interruption.

The conduct of {target} should be examined against the strike call itself. This paper does not assign unreported demands or assume the participation and outcome of the labour action announced here. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.
